topic_concept: Image Formation and Aperture of Convex Lens
question_text: A student forms a sharp image of a lighted candle on a screen using a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. The lower half of the lens is now covered with black paper. What happens to the image on the screen?
correct_answer_and_steps: The image remains completely intact and full. Every exposed portion of the lens refracts light rays from all parts of the object. Covering half the lens reduces the light energy transmitted, decreasing brightness without cropping.
student_response: The top half of the candle image is completely missing because the bottom half of the lens is covered.
evidence_rationale: Believes covering half the lens cuts the image in half, misunderstanding that every point on the lens receives light from every point on the object.
diagram_description: Convex lens with lower half covered by black opaque cardboard. Object placed beyond 2F forms a complete real inverted image on the screen with reduced brightness.

topic_concept: Real Image Formation in Space
question_text: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm focuses the image of a candle on a white screen placed 40 cm away. If the screen is abruptly removed, does the image still exist in space at that location?
correct_answer_and_steps: The real inverted image still exists in empty space at that exact focal position (aerial image). The screen merely scatters light diffusely so observers can view it from all angles; the convergence of light rays occurs independently of the screen.

misconception_label: MISC-OPT-002: Screen Reification (Image Exists Only on Screen)
evidence_rationale: Believes a real image is a physical drawing that only exists if a physical screen is present to capture it; does not understand that rays intersect in space forming an aerial image.
diagram_description: Convex lens forming real image in air. Cardboard screen is removed, showing rays still converge at the focal plane.

diagram_description: Concave mirror with optical center at origin. Object at u = -30 cm, f = -15 cm. Image forms at v = -30 cm.

question_text: A light ray enters a rectangular glass slab with parallel opposite faces at an angle of incidence of 45°. Describe the direction of the emergent ray relative to the incident ray.
correct_answer_and_steps: The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray (angle of emergence e equals angle of incidence i: e = i). The ray undergoes only a lateral displacement (sideways shift), not an angular deviation, because the opposing refracting surfaces are strictly parallel.

correct_answer_and_steps: The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray (angle of emergence e equals angle of incidence i: e = i). The ray undergoes only a lateral displacement (sideways shift), not an angular deviation, because the opposing refracting surfaces are strictly parallel.

misconception_label: MISC-OPT-005: Glass Slab Angular Deviation Fallacy

diagram_description: Rectangular glass slab showing incident ray at angle i, refraction at angle r, and emergent ray at angle e = i parallel to incident ray with lateral displacement d.

question_text: A person with myopia has a far point of 1.5 m. What kind of corrective lens must be prescribed, and what is its optical nature according to NCERT?
correct_answer_and_steps: The defect is Myopia (near-sightedness). The eye lens is too converging (or eyeball is elongated), causing distant rays to focus IN FRONT of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens is required to diverge the rays so they focus sharply on the retina.

question_text: A person with myopia has a far point of 1.5 m. What kind of corrective lens must be prescribed, and what is its optical nature according to NCERT?
correct_answer_and_steps: The defect is Myopia (near-sightedness). The eye lens is too converging (or eyeball is elongated), causing distant rays to focus IN FRONT of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens is required to diverge the rays so they focus sharply on the retina.
student_response: From what I understood, the student suffers from myopia; a diverging (concave) lens of focal length -100 cm restores vision.
evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.
diagram_description: Myopic eye forming image in front of retina, with concave corrective lens diverging rays to focus exactly on retina.

question_text: A person with myopia has a far point of 1.5 m. What kind of corrective lens must be prescribed, and what is its optical nature according to NCERT?
correct_answer_and_steps: The defect is Myopia (near-sightedness). The eye lens is too converging (or eyeball is elongated), causing distant rays to focus IN FRONT of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens is required to diverge the rays so they focus sharply on the retina.
student_response: Myopia: rays focus in front of retina. A concave lens is needed to diverge incoming parallel rays so they appear to come from the far point.
evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.
diagram_description: Myopic eye forming image in front of retina, with concave corrective lens diverging rays to focus exactly on retina.

question_text: A narrow beam of white light passes through a triangular glass prism. Which constituent color undergoes the greatest deviation from its original path?
correct_answer_and_steps: Violet light undergoes the greatest deviation. In glass, refractive index depends on wavelength (Cauchy's relation: n_violet > n_red). Red light travels fastest (v = c/n) and deviates least; violet travels slowest and bends most towards the prism base.

misconception_label: MISC-EYE-002: Prism Dispersion Speed and Deviation Inversion
evidence_rationale: Believes red light is deflected most or that red travels slowest in glass, inverting the Cauchy dispersion relation.
diagram_description: Equilateral glass prism with white light incident. Red refracts least (top of band), Violet refracts most (bottom of band).

topic_concept: Atmospheric Refraction (Twinkling of Stars)
question_text: Why do stars twinkle at night when viewed from Earth, whereas planets do not twinkle?
correct_answer_and_steps: Twinkling is caused by atmospheric refraction through turbulent, continuously shifting air layers with fluctuating temperatures and refractive indices. Because stars are distant point sources, small refractive deflections cause noticeable wavering in apparent position and brightness. Planets are extended sources, so point fluctuations average out.

evidence_rationale: Believes stars twinkle because of physical flickering, burning bursts, or cloud obstruction, rather than atmospheric refraction of point sources.
diagram_description: Light from distant star passing through turbulent atmospheric layers of varying density into observer's eye.

The intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength (I ~ 1/lambda^4). Shorter blue wavelengths scatter roughly 16 times more strongly than red, illuminating the sky blue from all directions.

evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.
diagram_description: Sunlight striking atmospheric gas molecules. Blue light scatters in all directions (I ~ 1/lambda^4); red transmits through.

question_text: Why does the clear daytime sky appear blue to an observer on Earth, but appears dark black to an astronaut in space without an atmosphere?
correct_answer_and_steps: Rayleigh scattering by atmospheric gas molecules (N2, O2) whose size is smaller than visible wavelengths. The intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength (I ~ 1/lambda^4). Shorter blue wavelengths scatter roughly 16 times more strongly than red, illuminating the sky blue from all directions.
student_response: Correctly identified blue scattering, but stated red light has higher frequency than blue.
evidence_rationale: Conceptual formula choice is correct; error is isolated to an arithmetic slip.
diagram_description: Sunlight striking atmospheric gas molecules. Blue light scatters in all directions (I ~ 1/lambda^4); red transmits through.

correct_answer_and_steps: Brightness of B1 is UNCHANGED. The battery maintains a constant potential difference V across each parallel branch (V1 = V2 = V). Current in branch 1 remains I1 = V/R. Adding branch 2 lowers the total equivalent resistance (R_eq = R/2), so the battery supplies TWICE the total current (I_total = 2I).
student_response: Bulb B1 dims to half brightness because the battery provides a fixed total current that must now be shared.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-002: Battery as Constant Current Source
evidence_rationale: Believes a battery produces a fixed constant total current regardless of what external resistance network is connected.
diagram_description: Battery connected to Bulb 1. A second identical Bulb 2 is connected in parallel via a switch. Battery delivers twice the current when switch closes.

correct_answer_and_steps: By Ohm's Law: I = V / R. Current is determined by the ratio of voltage to resistance. Increasing both proportionally keeps current constant.
student_response: Adding resistance always reduces I even if voltage goes up.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-003: Resistance Reduces Current Independent of Voltage
evidence_rationale: Believes that increasing resistance always reduces current even when voltage is simultaneously increased proportionally; fails to apply V = IR as a ratio relationship.
diagram_description: Simple circuit with variable resistor and voltmeter/ammeter showing V, I, R relationships.

correct_answer_and_steps: Zero force. The magnetic force on a charged particle is given by the Lorentz force equation F = q * (v x B) = q * v * B * sin(theta). evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.

correct_answer_and_steps: No EMF is induced (EMF = 0 V). Faraday's Law states EMF = -N * dPhi/dt. A constant (non-changing) magnetic field produces zero rate of change of magnetic flux (dPhi/dt = 0), so induced EMF is strictly zero.
student_response: in my opinion, as long as a strong magnet is present inside the coil, a steady potential diff is continuously generated even if nothing moves na sir.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-006: Static Field Induces Constant EMF Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes that a static (non-changing) magnetic field inside a coil continuously induces an EMF, not realizing that only a changing magnetic flux induces an EMF.
diagram_description: A coil placed inside a solenoid showing changing vs static magnetic flux and galvanometer deflection.

correct_answer_and_steps: Acceleration is 0 m/s^2. Acceleration is the RATE OF CHANGE of velocity: a = (v - u) / t. Because velocity is constant and direction is unchanged, delta v = 0, so acceleration is strictly zero regardless of how high the speed is.
student_response: Basically what happens is a train traveling at a high steady velocity of 30 m/s must have a huge acceleration because it is moving so fast.
evidence_rationale: Equates high speed with high acceleration; believes a vehicle moving at high constant speed must have large acceleration.
diagram_description: Velocity-time graph showing horizontal line for constant velocity v = 20 m/s. Slope a = dv/dt = 0.

misconception_label: MISC-WRK-001: Work Equals Force Times Distance Regardless of Direction
evidence_rationale: Applies W = F * d without considering the angle between force and displacement; believes work is done whenever force is applied even if perpendicular to motion.

correct_answer_and_steps: Voltage does NOT flow. Voltage (electric potential difference) exists ACROSS two points and represents the work done per unit charge (V = W/Q) driving the circuit. Current (I) is the actual physical flow of electric charge THROUGH a conductor. Current flows through; voltage is applied across.

evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.
diagram_description: Circuit with voltmeter across resistor (measuring across two points) and ammeter in series (measuring through one line).

correct_answer_and_steps: Resistance is halved (R' = R/2) because R is directly proportional to length (R = rho * L / A). However, resistivity rho remains STRICTLY UNCHANGED. Resistivity is an intrinsic material property that depends only on the chemical nature of the substance and temperature, not on length, area, or shape.
student_response: Resistivity decreases since a shorter wire has less material to resist.
evidence_rationale: Believes resistivity (rho) depends on the dimensions (length or area) of a wire, wrongly concluding that cutting a wire in half halves its resistivity.
diagram_description: Cylindrical copper wire of length L and cross-section A cut in half into length L/2. Resistance is halved (R/2); resistivity rho remains strictly identical.

correct_answer_and_steps: Resistance is halved (R' = R/2) because R is directly proportional to length (R = rho * L / A). However, resistivity rho remains STRICTLY UNCHANGED. Resistivity is an intrinsic material property that depends only on the chemical nature of the substance and temperature, not on length, area, or shape.
student_response: Resistivity does not change at all; only the resistance depends on length and cross-sectional area (R = rho*L/A).
evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.

correct_answer_and_steps: Resistance is halved (R' = R/2) because R is directly proportional to length (R = rho * L / A). However, resistivity rho remains STRICTLY UNCHANGED. Resistivity is an intrinsic material property that depends only on the chemical nature of the substance and temperature, not on length, area, or shape.
student_response: Stated rho is unchanged, but calculated new resistance of stretched wire as 2R instead of 4R (neglecting volume conservation).
evidence_rationale: Conceptual formula choice is correct; error is isolated to an arithmetic slip.
diagram_description: Cylindrical copper wire of length L and cross-section A cut in half into length L/2. Resistance is halved (R/2); resistivity rho remains strictly identical.

topic_concept: Short Circuit and Parallel Branch Current Distribution
question_text: A lighted bulb is connected to a battery. A thick copper wire of negligible resistance is now connected directly across the two terminals of the bulb. What happens to the bulb?
correct_answer_and_steps: The bulb turns OFF completely (goes dark). The ideal wire has virtually zero resistance (R = 0). In parallel, current divides inversely proportional to resistance (I_bulb / I_wire = R_wire / R_bulb = 0). Practically 100% of the current flows through the bypass wire, short-circuiting the bulb so zero current flows through its filament.

misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-008: Zero-Resistance Short Circuit Current Sharing Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes current continues to divide equally through a bulb when a zero-resistance wire is connected in parallel across it, failing to recognize complete bypass (short circuit).
diagram_description: Bulb connected to battery. An ideal zero-resistance jumper wire connects the two terminals of the bulb. All current bypasses the bulb, so it turns off completely.

topic_concept: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor in a Magnetic Field
question_text: A straight wire carrying current is placed inside a uniform magnetic field. Can the magnetic force on the wire ever be in the same direction as the magnetic field lines?
correct_answer_and_steps: No, the magnetic force is NEVER parallel to the magnetic field lines. By the Lorentz force rule F = I * (L x B) = I * L * B * sin(theta), the magnetic force is mutually perpendicular to both the conductor (current) and the magnetic field. When current is parallel to field (theta = 0), sin(0) = 0, so force is zero.

misconception_label: MISC-MAG-003: Magnetic Force Collinear / Parallel Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes the magnetic force on a current-carrying wire acts parallel to the magnetic field lines, failing to understand that magnetic force is strictly perpendicular to both field and current.

correct_answer_and_steps: No, the magnetic force is NEVER parallel to the magnetic field lines. By the Lorentz force rule F = I * (L x B) = I * L * B * sin(theta), the magnetic force is mutually perpendicular to both the conductor (current) and the magnetic field. When current is parallel to field (theta = 0), sin(0) = 0, so force is zero.
student_response: My intuition says a current-carrying wire placed in a magnetic field experiences a force that pulls it directly along the direction of the magnetic field lines.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-003: Magnetic Force Collinear / Parallel Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes the magnetic force on a current-carrying wire acts parallel to the magnetic field lines, failing to understand that magnetic force is strictly perpendicular to both field and current.
diagram_description: Horizontal wire in horizontal magnetic field. Magnetic force F acts vertically (perpendicular to both I and B via cross product).

correct_answer_and_steps: No, the magnetic force is NEVER parallel to the magnetic field lines. By the Lorentz force rule F = I * (L x B) = I * L * B * sin(theta), the magnetic force is mutually perpendicular to both the conductor (current) and the magnetic field. When current is parallel to field (theta = 0), sin(0) = 0, so force is zero.
student_response: My intuition says a current-carrying wire placed in a magnetic field experiences a force that pulls it directly along the direction of the magnetic field lines.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-003: Magnetic Force Collinear / Parallel Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes the magnetic force on a current-carrying wire acts parallel to the magnetic field lines, failing to understand that magnetic force is strictly perpendicular to both field and current.
diagram_description: Horizontal wire in horizontal magnetic field. Magnetic force F acts vertically (perpendicular to both I and B via cross product).

correct_answer_and_steps: No, the magnetic force is NEVER parallel to the magnetic field lines. By the Lorentz force rule F = I * (L x B) = I * L * B * sin(theta), the magnetic force is mutually perpendicular to both the conductor (current) and the magnetic field. When current is parallel to field (theta = 0), sin(0) = 0, so force is zero.
student_response: When wire is parallel to field, theta = 0, giving F = ILB sin(0) = 0 N. Magnetic force is perpendicular to B, never parallel.
evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.
diagram_description: Horizontal wire in horizontal magnetic field. Magnetic force F acts vertically (perpendicular to both I and B via cross product).

correct_answer_and_steps: Distance = 44 m (circumference = 2 * pi * r = 2 * (22/7) * 7 = 44 m). Displacement = 0 m. Distance is the total scalar path length traveled. evidence_rationale: Believes distance and displacement are always identical scalar quantities, failing to understand that displacement is a vector from initial to final position and can be zero after a round trip.

topic_concept: Acceleration: Sign of Acceleration and Direction of Motion
question_text: A car travels towards the West (chosen as negative direction) with velocity -15 m/s and has an acceleration of -3 m/s^2. Is the car speeding up or slowing down?
correct_answer_and_steps: The car is SPEEDING UP. Whether an object speeds up or slows down depends on the relative signs of velocity and acceleration, not the sign of acceleration alone. When velocity and acceleration have the SAME sign (both negative), the object speeds up in the negative direction. Deceleration (slowing down) occurs ONLY when velocity and acceleration have OPPOSITE signs.

topic_concept: Average Speed for Equal Distance Intervals
question_text: A car travels from town A to town B at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns from B to A along the same route at 40 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire round trip?
correct_answer_and_steps: Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2d / (d/60 + d/40) = 2*60*40 / (60+40) = 4800 / 100 = 48 km/h. Average speed is NOT the arithmetic average (60+40)/2 = 50 km/h, because more time is spent traveling at the slower speed.

evidence_rationale: Calculates average speed for equal distances as the simple arithmetic average (v1 + v2) / 2 instead of total distance divided by total time (harmonic mean 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2)).

topic_concept: Mass and Weight
question_text: An astronaut has a mass of 60 kg on Earth. What will be the astronaut's mass and weight on the surface of the Moon, where acceleration due to gravity is 1/6th of Earth's (g_moon = 1.63 m/s^2)?
correct_answer_and_steps: Mass on Moon = 60 kg (UNCHANGED). Weight on Moon = m * g_moon = 60 * 1.63 = 98 N (or 588 / 6 = 98 N). Mass is the measure of inertia and quantity of matter; it is strictly invariant everywhere in the universe. Weight is the gravitational force exerted on the object (W = mg), which varies with local gravity.

diagram_description: Astronaut on Earth (m=60 kg, W=588 N) and on Moon (m=60 kg, W=98 N). Mass is invariant; weight is location-dependent force.

correct_answer_and_steps: Mass on Moon = 60 kg (UNCHANGED). Weight on Moon = m * g_moon = 60 * 1.63 = 98 N (or 588 / 6 = 98 N). Mass is the measure of inertia and quantity of matter; it is strictly invariant everywhere in the universe. Weight is the gravitational force exerted on the object (W = mg), which varies with local gravity.
student_response: wait sir, mass drops to 10 kg because there is less gravity to hold the mass together pakka.
evidence_rationale: Conflates mass and weight, believing that an object's mass changes when taken to the Moon, or treating weight as a scalar intrinsic property measured in kilograms.
diagram_description: Astronaut on Earth (m=60 kg, W=588 N) and on Moon (m=60 kg, W=98 N). Mass is invariant; weight is location-dependent force.

correct_answer_and_steps: Mass on Moon = 60 kg (UNCHANGED). Weight on Moon = m * g_moon = 60 * 1.63 = 98 N (or 588 / 6 = 98 N). Mass is the measure of inertia and quantity of matter; it is strictly invariant everywhere in the universe. Weight is the gravitational force exerted on the object (W = mg), which varies with local gravity.
student_response: I feel like an astronaut on the Moon has less mass than on Earth because the Moon's gravity is only 1/6th of Earth's gravity.
evidence_rationale: Conflates mass and weight, believing that an object's mass changes when taken to the Moon, or treating weight as a scalar intrinsic property measured in kilograms.
diagram_description: Astronaut on Earth (m=60 kg, W=588 N) and on Moon (m=60 kg, W=98 N). Mass is invariant; weight is location-dependent force.

question_text: The gravitational force between two identical spheres separated by distance r is 100 N. If the distance between their centers is doubled to 2r, what is the new gravitational force?

evidence_rationale: Treats gravitational force as inversely proportional to distance (1/r) rather than distance squared (1/r^2), wrongly concluding that doubling distance cuts force in half.

diagram_description: Two masses separated by distance r (force F). When separation is increased to 2r, force drops to F/4.

question_text: A moving automobile of mass 1000 kg has a kinetic energy of 50,000 J at 10 m/s. If its speed is doubled to 20 m/s, what is its new kinetic energy?
correct_answer_and_steps: The new kinetic energy is 200,000 J (quadrupled: 4 * 50,000 J = 200,000 J). Kinetic energy is proportional to the SQUARE of velocity: E_k = (1/2) * m * v^2. Doubling speed multiplies kinetic energy by 2^2 = 4, which is why braking distance also quadruples.

misconception_label: MISC-ENG-001: Kinetic Energy Velocity Linearity Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes kinetic energy is directly proportional to velocity (linear) rather than velocity squared (quadratic), wrongly concluding that doubling speed doubles kinetic energy.

correct_answer_and_steps: The new kinetic energy is 200,000 J (quadrupled: 4 * 50,000 J = 200,000 J). Kinetic energy is proportional to the SQUARE of velocity: E_k = (1/2) * m * v^2. Doubling speed multiplies kinetic energy by 2^2 = 4, which is why braking distance also quadruples.
student_response: New kinetic energy is 100,000 J because doubling speed doubles kinetic energy (2 * 50,000 = 100,000 J).
misconception_label: MISC-ENG-001: Kinetic Energy Velocity Linearity Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes kinetic energy is directly proportional to velocity (linear) rather than velocity squared (quadratic), wrongly concluding that doubling speed doubles kinetic energy.
diagram_description: Car moving at speed v (kinetic energy E_k). When speed doubles to 2v, kinetic energy increases fourfold (4*E_k), requiring 4x the braking distance.

topic_concept: Work Done by Centripetal / Gravitational Force in Circular Motion
question_text: A satellite orbits the Earth in a circular path at a constant speed of 7 km/s. What is the total work done by Earth's gravitational force on the satellite in one complete revolution?
correct_answer_and_steps: Work done is strictly 0 J. Gravitational force acts radially inward towards Earth's center, while the instantaneous displacement of the satellite is tangential along the circle. The angle between force and displacement is always 90 degrees. Since W = F * d * cos(90 deg) = 0, gravity does zero work on the satellite, keeping its kinetic energy constant.

misconception_label: MISC-WRK-002: Circular Orbit Gravitational Work Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes gravitational force does continuous positive work on a planet or satellite in a circular orbit to keep it moving around the Sun/Earth.
diagram_description: Satellite orbiting Earth in circular orbit. Gravitational force points towards center; instantaneous displacement is tangential (theta = 90 deg). Net work is 0 J.
